newsitem.title: FRANCE: French export insurance agency Coface profits up.
newsitem.headline: French export insurance agency Coface profits up.

text.p: French export insurance agency Coface said on Tuesday that 1996 net consolidated profit jumped 19 percent to 246 million francs from 207 million in 1995.
The agency which covers corporate financial risk in the international markets reported turnover rose by 16 percent to 2.86 billion francs.
Turnover rose 10 percent excluding acquisition effects.

The group noted that at the start of 1997, French insurer AGF had increased its direct stake in Coface to 41.7 percent and now controlled indirectly 58 percent of the company's equity "in keeping with the credit insurance development policy of AGF."

The credit insurance managed by Coface on behalf of the French state generated a 5.1 billion franc surplus after a return to breakeven the previous year. For the first time in 15 years, premium income exceeded insurance claims.
It said in a statement that the surplus was due partly to the improved financial situation of debtor countries.
It said 1997 "augured well for the expansion of the Coface group."
The improved business environment in western Europe "gives us good reason to export exports to hold up well and for claim levels to remain reasonable," it said.
It said that uncertainties about the dollar had led to renewed interest in foreign currency cover.
